sections.h2: What should a Nebraska home seller know about the state as a whole?
sections.html:
Nebraska is a low-density state with two large metro areas on the eastern edge. The Census Bureau counts 2,018,006 residents as of July 1, 2025, spread over 76,817.87 square miles of land, which works out to 25.5 people per square mile in the 2020 data.

Most of that population sits in a few counties. Douglas County, which holds Omaha, is estimated at 606,460 and Sarpy County, just south of it, at 208,303. Sarpy grew 9.3% between April 2020 and July 2025, against 3.8% for Douglas and 2.9% for the state.

Housing across the state looks different from one county to the next, which is why a seller in Papillion and a seller in a small western town face different questions. The same house can be priced, taxed and sold on very different timelines depending on where it sits.

sections.h2: How do Douglas, Sarpy and the state compare?
sections.html:
Sarpy County has the highest median owner-occupied home value of the three at $314,100, followed by Douglas at $266,100 and the state at $238,600, per the 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey estimates.

Census figures for cities put Omaha at 488,797, Lincoln at 301,522 and Bellevue at 64,863 for July 2025. Lincoln is the state capital and sits in Lancaster County, one of the three counties the state treats as large for tax deadlines.

sections.h2: What are Nebraska's main regions, and why do they matter for a house?
sections.html:
The two big metro areas sit in the east, while the middle of the state holds the Sandhills. The Game and Parks Commission says the Sandhills cover 19,300 square miles, almost a quarter of the state, and describes them as a land with far fewer people than cattle and few roads.

For sellers the practical differences are these:

  • In the Omaha and Lincoln corridors, a house is one of many nearby sales and a county assessor tracks a large, active roll.
  • In small towns and rural counties, there are fewer comparable sales, and a buyer pool may be limited to people already in the area.
  • Acreage and farm ground follow different assessment rules, covered in the property tax section below.

Each county runs its own assessor, treasurer, register of deeds and county court, so a guide that says "Nebraska" usually points you back to a county office for the specific step.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Nebraska?
sections.html:
Nebraska property tax is valued by the county assessor, set by the local taxing bodies and collected by the county treasurer. All taxes are due on December 31, and the first half becomes delinquent on May 1 and the second half on September 1.

Douglas, Lancaster and Sarpy counties run on a faster schedule: the first half is delinquent on April 1 and the second half on August 1. The Department of Revenue's calendar defines the longer schedule for counties under 100,000 people, which is every county except those three.

StepDate
Valuation dateJanuary 1, 12:01 a.m.
Valuation change notices mailedOn or before June 1
Protest window with county board of equalizationJune 1 to June 30
Homestead exemption applicationsAfter February 1 and by June 30
Tax levies setOn or before October 15
Taxes dueDecember 31

Real property is assessed at or near 100% of actual value, while agricultural and horticultural land is assessed at or near 75%. The assessor does not set tax rates or collect the tax.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when a Nebraska house is sold?
sections.html:
The tax for a given year is due December 31 and is paid to the county treasurer, so a closing in spring or summer usually has a half-year or more of tax that is already due or about to become delinquent. Ask the title company which year and which half is open on your parcel.

Homestead exemptions are tied to who occupies the home, and the state says applications run annually. A seller who is over 65, disabled or in another qualifying group may already have an exemption on file, so ask the county assessor how a sale affects it.

Our statewide Nebraska property tax guide and the county guides listed on this page go into appeals and exemptions in more depth. A valuation protest must be in writing, signed and filed with the county clerk by June 30.

sections.h2: What are the steps to record a Nebraska deed?
sections.html:
A deed is recorded with the county register of deeds, and the grantee must file a completed Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, at the same time. Under Neb. Rev. Stat. 76-214, the register must refuse to record the deed if the statement is missing.

The register of deeds forwards the statement to the county assessor, who passes it to the Tax Commissioner. The documentary stamp tax is also collected at recording. As of July 18, 2026, the rate is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value or fraction of $1,000, and before that date it was $2.32.

  • Deeds between spouses or parent and child without actual consideration are exempt.
  • Deeds of distribution from a personal representative are exempt.
  • Transfer on death deeds and revocations of them are exempt.
  • Deeds given in lieu of foreclosure to release a debt are exempt.

A trustee's deed issued after a power of sale is exercised is not exempt.

sections.h2: How do inherited houses move in Nebraska?
sections.html:
Heirs can use probate, a transfer on death deed or, for a small estate, a short affidavit filed with the register of deeds. The affidavit route requires 30 days since death, no personal representative, real property worth $100,000 or less on the assessment rolls after taxes due, and signatures from every other heir.

Inheritance tax is a county matter. Nebraska charges the person who receives property under rates of 1%, 11% and 15% by relationship, and the county court determines the tax. The tax is due 12 months after death, and interest and penalties can build after that. See our estate and inheritance tax guide for the exempt amounts and a worked example.

A county treasurer receives the Form PCIT report after the court order, which is one reason an inherited house sale can involve the treasurer, the court and the register of deeds on the same file.

sections.h2: Which Nebraska offices will a seller actually deal with?
sections.html:
Most steps run through a handful of county and state offices, and the guides on this page are organized around the ones you will meet first.

  • County assessor: valuation, homestead applications and parcel records. The Department of Revenue keeps a directory of every county assessor.
  • County treasurer: property tax payments and inheritance tax payments.
  • County clerk: valuation protests for the board of equalization.
  • Register of deeds: recording deeds, affidavits and the transfer statement.
  • County court: probate and inheritance tax determination.
  • Department of Revenue: rate tables, forms 521 and PCIT, and statewide calendars.

Use the city guides above for local selling questions and the county guides for property tax details. The statewide guides cover rules that apply the same way everywhere in Nebraska, such as the deed recording requirements and the inheritance tax classes.

faqs.q: What are the largest cities in Nebraska?
faqs.a: Omaha is the largest at 488,797 people, then Lincoln at 301,522 and Bellevue at 64,863, according to the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimates.

faqs.q: When are Nebraska property taxes due?
faqs.a: All taxes are due December 31. In most counties the first half is delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1. In Douglas, Lancaster and Sarpy counties the dates are April 1 and August 1.

faqs.q: Who sets my property's value in Nebraska?
faqs.a: The county assessor values real property as of January 1 each year. If you disagree, file a written protest with the county board of equalization through the county clerk between June 1 and June 30.

faqs.q: What form is needed to record a deed in Nebraska?
faqs.a: The grantee files a Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521, with the register of deeds. The register cannot record the deed without it.

faqs.q: How much is the Nebraska documentary stamp tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. Before that date the rate was $2.32 per $1,000.

faqs.q: Can I transfer an inherited house without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If 30 days have passed, no personal representative exists, the Nebraska real property is worth $100,000 or less on the assessment rolls and the other heirs sign, an affidavit filed with the register of deeds can transfer it.

faqs.q: Are farm and ranch parcels assessed the same as houses?
faqs.a: No. Real property is assessed at or near 100% of actual value, but agricultural and horticultural land is assessed at or near 75%.
